text:
**continue**: the claim holds on this board and the check catches its break. Before M9, the orchestrator should run the Harmonize dry runs that M5, M7 and M8 all left pending as one subagent pass and fill each post's `real_project`.

## Holds
- **Sampled bar, rerun:** "second orchestrator resume, nothing new: 93 vs 21,633 characters". I ran the step's `kit.py` (the review branch's `.kit/kit.py` is byte-identical to `scripts/kit.py` at 6b20a2f) on this board under a fresh session id: first `resume --role orchestrator`, then a second one, then `--full`. Output: **24,859 / 93 / 24,859 characters**, all exit 0. The second one is one line, `Resume: nothing new since 21:51 UTC (the whole: kit.py resume --role orchestrator --full)`. The 93 matches exactly. The whole has grown since the step measured it (21,633 → 24,859, because the board gained posts), so the ratio is now 0.37% rather than 0.4%. `--full` after a delta printed the same size as the first whole one. I deleted my test state file afterwards.
- **Check:** `python3 -m unittest tests.test_resume_delta` in a worktree at 6b20a2f: 12 of 12 pass.
- **Breaks:** applied `RESUME_DELTA_ROLES = ()` in the worktree. The check then fails (2 failures, 6 errors). Undone; the tree is clean. So the check can fail.
- **Not checked:** the one-new-comment bar (204 characters). Measuring it means writing a comment on the shared board, and the test suite covers each of the five kinds of change. I also did not check agy compaction, which the post lists as not_checked.
- **Real project:** the post has **no `real_project`**. K2 makes that mandatory for a change to resume, so this step is not fully done until the orchestrator runs it on anlonlt/harmonize.

## Goal
- The train's goal: "any session understands any project quickly". M5 serves the cost side of that: a re-read before each answer goes from about 25k characters to under 100. Characters stand in for tokens. It is a fair stand-in here, because the output is plain text.
- **Pattern across posts:** M5, M7 and M8 each name the Harmonize run as "the orchestrator's" in `not_checked`, and none of them has a `real_project` yet. That makes three deferrals of the same K2 check in a row. The lesson exists because CL29 passed the kit's own suite and still broke Harmonize.
- **Known-good case / owner try:** the only owner input on this train is the map design (comment `m1-owner-map-design`). No owner try of M5–M8 is recorded, which makes four Dones without one. For M5 he cannot see the result himself: it changes what the orchestrator reads. So the try that counts here is the real-project run.

## Verdict
**continue.** The step does what it claims, and its check can fail.
Suggestion: before launching M9, one orchestrator subagent clones anlonlt/harmonize (never pushed) and runs: `kit.py resume --role orchestrator` twice with one session id (M5), then `kit.py lessons check` (M7/M8). It writes each command and its output into the three posts' `real_project`.
